key_insight: Pixel-space diffusion models can scale effectively with LLM-style Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), breaking the usual tradeoff between model size and active compute. PixelMoE shows that sparse expert routing can boost capacity without making every token/image patch expensive to process.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of scaling pixel-space diffusion models efficiently. Traditional dense scaling increases compute for every part of the model, making it hard to grow capacity without a large cost in training and inference.
method: Transfers standard LLM-style Mixture-of-Experts architecture into pixel-space diffusion models.
Uses sparse expert activation so only a subset of experts is used per input, increasing total model capacity without proportional compute growth.
Introduces PixelMoE as a scalable design for modeling raw images directly, avoiding dependence on learned tokenizers.
impact: For practitioners, PixelMoE offers a path to build larger, more expressive image diffusion models while keeping compute more manageable. This could improve image generation quality and efficiency, especially for large-scale training setups.

paper_title: PixelMoE: Scaling Pixel-Space Diffusion with LLM-Style Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Ruixiao Dong, Jianmin Bao, Bozhi Luan, Zijie Meng, Xin Tao
